title: Keldysh field theory of spin- and valley-distinguished polariton nonlinearities in transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers
authors: Anna M. Grudinina, Nina S. Voronova
abstract: Electrons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) possess valley and spin degrees of freedom, which leads to rich exciton and exciton-polariton physics with nontrivial scattering dynamics and enhanced nonlinearities, presenting a key mechanism for photonic devices. Yet, existing descriptions of bosonization and polariton interactions in TMD-based systems overlook the valley degree of freedom as well as the various particles' spins combinations. In this work, we derive a nonequilibrium field-theory approach in the path integral formalism that allows to track all the polariton nonlinearities in the strong coupling regime. We demonstrate that, when all the bright and dark exciton species are considered, the TMD monolayer-based polariton systems feature sixteen different nonlinear contributions due to interactions and even more saturation-related terms. Strikingly, while the interactions of excitons within one valley are overall dominant, we show that the contribution to the blueshift from spin-dark excitons is much higher than that from bright intravalley excitons.
summary: The paper develops an advanced Keldysh field theory approach to model polariton nonlinearities in TMD monolayers, explicitly accounting for spin and valley degrees of freedom. It calculates numerous interaction terms, revealing that previously overlooked dark exciton contributions can dominate optical shifts. This work is vital for predicting the behavior of quantum light sources in 2D materials.
main_problem: To derive a comprehensive, non-equilibrium field-theory description of all polariton nonlinearities in transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers by fully incorporating the valley and spin degrees of freedom.
main_result: The full consideration reveals sixteen distinct nonlinear contributions; notably, the blueshift contribution from spin-dark excitons can exceed that from bright intravalley excitons.
method: The authors employ Keldysh field theory in the path integral formalism to derive interaction and saturation terms ($\Delta \mathcal{S}$) for the exciton-photon system.
model_or_system: The physical system is TMD monolayers (like $	ext{WS}_2$) exhibiting strong light-matter coupling, leading to exciton-polaritons. The model incorporates valley ($	ext{K}, 	ext{K}'$) and spin ($\uparrow, \downarrow$) degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Polariton nonlinearities ($g_{	ext{ex}}, g_{	ext{sat}}$), blueshift contributions, and interaction matrix elements for various exciton species (bright/dark).
important_parameters: Low temperature ($T=0$), strong coupling regime, valley indices ($\lambda$), spin projections ($\sigma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the low-density limit in some derivations and neglects electron-hole exchange interactions between different valleys.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the band structure near K/K' points. Figure 2 plots calculated matrix elements for four types of exciton interactions (intravalley, intervalley, etc.).
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the general non-equilibrium action using path integrals, systematically derives nonlinear interaction terms by considering all spin/valley combinations, and finally analyzes specific contributions like screening corrections and saturation effects.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed theoretical framework for understanding complex many-body interactions in solid-state quantum emitters, which is crucial for designing next-generation photonic devices based on strong light-matter coupling.
